summary: Asana requires app registration via the developer console to obtain credentials. Developers must implement OAuth 2.0 with PKCE for secure access. Public distribution requires a formal submission process, including providing support documentation and passing a review.

go_public.item: You must submit your app for review to make it available to users in any Asana workspace…

claim.text: You must submit your app for review to make it available to users in any Asana workspace beyond your own or to list it publicly.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Submitting your app for review is not required to obtain a token. You only need to submit your app if you intend to: Make your app available to users in any Asana workspace, beyond your own organization or development environment List your app publicly on the Asana app directory

claim.text: You must provide test account credentials for the review process.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Provide any test account credentials necessary for your app (this is only used for the review process and will not be published publicly)

claim.text: You must provide a privacy policy URL.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Include a privacy policy URL to ensure transparency about how you handle user data and comply with legal requirements.

claim.text: You must provide a support page URL or email.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Include a support page URL or email for users who need help troubleshooting the app.

claim.text: You must provide an app landing or login page URL.
claim.label: official_docs

claim.text: Apps submitted for publication to the app directory must be shared to Any workspace.

claim.text: Search API calls are limited to 60 requests per minute.

blockers.issue: Non-native applications must use https for redirect URLs.
blockers.fix: Use an https URL for the redirect endpoint.

claim.text: Non-native applications must use https for redirect URLs.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: For security reasons, non-native applications must supply a "https" URL (more on this below).

blockers.issue: Requests to the authorization endpoint without PKCE will be rejected if using localhost,…
blockers.fix: Include a code_challenge in the authorization request and the matching code_verifier in the token exchange.

claim.text: Requests to the authorization endpoint without PKCE will be rejected if using localhost, 127.0.0.1, or native URN redirect URIs.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: OAuth flows that use a localhost, 127.0.0.1, or native URN redirect URI must use PKCE (S256). Include a code_challenge in the authorization request and the matching code_verifier in the token exchange. Requests without these parameters will be rejected.

blockers.issue: Apps cannot be edited once they have been submitted for review.

claim.text: Apps cannot be edited once they have been submitted for review.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Once your app has been submitted on the Submit for review page, the review process will begin. At this point, the app will no longer be open for further edits.

blockers.issue: If you request a scope that is not in your app's approved list, the user will see a…
blockers.fix: Update the scopes your app is allowed to request by editing your app's settings in the developer console.

claim.text: If you request a scope that is not in your app's approved list, the user will see a forbidden_scopes error
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: If you request a scope that is not in your app's approved (i.e., registered) list, the user will see a forbidden_scopes error on the authorization page.

blockers.issue: If either the client_id or redirect_uri do not match, the user will simply see a…
blockers.fix: Ensure client_id and redirect_uri match the application settings.

claim.text: If either the client_id or redirect_uri do not match, the user will simply see a plain-text error
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: If either the client_id or redirect_uri do not match, the user will simply see a plain-text error.

blockers.issue: Requests without PKCE parameters will be rejected for localhost redirect URLs
blockers.fix: Include a code_challenge in the authorization request and the matching code_verifier in the token exchange.

claim.text: Requests without PKCE parameters will be rejected for localhost redirect URLs
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: OAuth flows that use a localhost, 127.0.0.1, or native URN redirect URI must use PKCE (S256). Include a code_challenge in the authorization request and the matching code_verifier in the token exchange. Requests without these parameters will be rejected.
